memo.verdict: Neutral; park, with a price trigger; conviction medium. The record does not invalidate the case and does not progress it. The gate does not park the case (no D or F on management at B, business quality at B, transmission at A or trackability at B); the return does. Progress to Early-Stage work if the shares fall toward 25 to 27 EUR (7.7x to 8.3x the current 24-month-forward earnings) with the liability margin still at or above 1.05 percent and the Q3 2026 print (29 to 31 October 2026) confirming the German deposit defence. Drop the case if the liability margin falls below 1.00 percent or ING raises its standard German savings rate, because then the earnings leg and the price leg fail together. The record's one-line bet: at 31 EUR we would be betting that the market keeps paying 9.4 times for a bank whose margin tailwind fades in 2028; we decline that bet and would take the earnings bet, which we believe, at about 25 EUR. The case clears the framework's 20 percent bar only below about 25 EUR; it is a B case at 25 EUR and a C case at 31 EUR on the same facts.
case: The thesis sentence: ING Groep is a 'Major Corporate Change' case riding a dated external tailwind, bought late. The earnings leg is probable for two years, because a contractual repricing of a 524 billion EUR hedge book and a set of internal changes that have all arrived early lift earnings per share about 16.5 percent a year to FY2028. At 31.035 EUR the shares already pay for that leg and pay nothing for the fade after it.

The external force. The euro retail replicating portfolio, 524 billion EUR and 6.7 times market capitalisation, reprices from a 1.85 percent yield in 2026 to 2.23 percent in 2027 and 2.41 percent in 2028 as legacy swaps mature into higher market swap rates. It has already lifted the liability margin from 1.04 to 1.07 percent in one quarter and commercial net interest income 10.7 percent year on year. The change-forces research rates it the highest-impact driver, with plausibility above 80 percent because the rollovers are mechanical, and a 1.4 billion EUR upward revision to 2027 replicating income. The step-up is contractual, which makes the earnings leg probable; it plateaus in 2028, which makes the return leg not. The ECB is raising to 2.50 percent in September 2026 with terminal pricing of 2.75 to 3 percent; Morgan Stanley's baseline then has the rate declining to 2.0 percent by 2027. The other external forces are mild headwinds or neutral: competition tightening in German and Italian deposits and Dutch mortgages (D); labour and technology inflating faster than revenue (D); regulation mixed, with Polish tax to 30 percent and higher levies against the Dutch mortgage risk-weight floor expiring 30 November 2026 for 20 to 30 basis points of CET1 (C); disruption a contest (C); demand a mid-single-digit cyclical upswing with ING's own volumes above outlook (C).

The internal forces. Six of twelve at B or better, no screen red flag: guidance raised twice in 2026 across five metrics with every June 2024 Capital Markets Day target lifted or reached early (A); shareholder returns stepped up (B); perimeter reduced, with Wholesale risk-weighted assets down 4.6 billion EUR and Retail at 56 percent of risk-weighted assets eighteen months early (B); balance-sheet utilisation rising on a stable capital ratio (B); three executive board seats changed in six months, with the new finance director expected to drive 2027 upgrades (B); standards improving from a weak base, with more than 750 FTEs down and about 1,250 operations FTEs to go (B); Wholesale bankers compensated on return on risk weight (B). No chief-executive change (D); strategy unchanged since mid-2024 (C). The leadership research's verdict, incremental optimisation rather than transformational repositioning, is accepted.
counter_case: The risks research's FALSE FRIEND profile, carried at full force at the head of the 'Investment Thesis' and in the Written Summary. ING's visible strengths, retail growth, digital scale and capital returns, conceal a structure that fails when the rate cycle turns, and the turn is nearer than the market thinks. The replicating portfolio is 6.7 times market capitalisation against 2 to 3 times at peers, and management shortened its reinvestment profile in late 2023 to 50 percent maturing within twelve months, the opposite of peers' counter-cyclical practice and an unexplained anomaly, so the book reprices faster than peers' in both directions; a parallel downward shock costs 1,075 million EUR of net interest income. 58 percent of deposits are savings accounts and only 25 percent current accounts, so deposit betas bite harder than at peers. Chase, BBVA and Revolut are buying share in exactly the markets, Germany, Spain and Italy, where ING is online-only and, per Morgan Stanley, more at risk than branch banks; Revolut has already overtaken ING's whole Spanish customer base, the first such overtaking of an incumbent in a core European retail market, and ING's displacement velocity is in the top 5 percent of European incumbents. The CET1 headroom is 10 basis points, the tightest in the Benelux cohort against ABN AMRO at 15.4 to 15.9 percent and KBC at 14.4 to 15 percent, so any risk-weighted-asset inflation stops the buyback; Deutsche Bank warns the total payout falls below the historical 80 percent on regulatory add-ons, and Jefferies says capital is no longer a differentiator. Cost-to-income is 300 to 700 basis points worse than peers' targets and cost-to-serve is four to five times a challenger's. Compliance findings recur: the 2018 anti-money-laundering settlement of 775 million EUR (24 basis points of CET1, 15 percent of a year's net income, 11 percent sector underperformance), the 2019 to 2020 Bank of Italy onboarding ban, Luxembourg cases referred to trial, the September 2026 Australian add-on of 50 million USD for a multi-year liquidity-coverage overstatement. The shares trade at the 92nd percentile of their five-year range while Jefferies and Morgan Stanley, the two houses closest to the margin debate, are Hold and Equal-weight and prefer ABN AMRO; the industry says the first-phase net interest income uplift is definitively over. On this reading the ECB returns to 2.0 percent in 2027 while German deposit competition forces rate matching, the liability margin falls back toward 100 basis points, FY2028 earnings land nearer 3.0 EUR than 3.35 EUR, and the multiple de-rates at the same time; the sell-side's own stressed values are 19 EUR (Jefferies, 12 percent cost of equity, 30 basis points cost of risk) to 25 EUR (Morgan Stanley bear, 12 percent return on tangible equity by 2027), 19 to 39 percent below the price. All the individually tolerable weaknesses, tight headroom, cost base, savings-heavy mix, pro-cyclical hedge book, Belgian share loss, recurring findings and a top-of-range multiple, bind together under a rate cut plus a German deposit war; that is the Pret sandwich the record marks partly present. The leadership research's moderate-to-low confidence in top-quartile returns says this management executes, it does not transform, and it will not out-run a rate cycle. At Building Block level the counter-case is sharper still: the right box is none of the six, because the case is a rate-cycle beneficiary dressed as self-help, and a pattern that mis-names the driver mis-times the exit; and a disciplined investor would simply buy the compounding, 16 percent earnings growth and a 4 to 5 percent yield, and accept 11 to 12 percent a year if the multiple holds.

The record's response. It concedes the exposure, its size, the 2023 duration anomaly, the deposit mix, the Spanish precedent, the tight headroom, that the valuation gives no cushion, that its own modal return is an F and its drop-through case removes even the D branch, and that the leadership reading is right. It holds that the earnings leg is probable for two years and the price leg is not, and that the hypothesis and the case agree on the second: the swap roll to 2.41 percent is contractual and sized by three houses; the ECB is raising into year-end 2026; Q2 2026 showed the franchise defending German deposits at 3.75 percent against a 4 percent teaser while expanding the margin 3 basis points and growing group deposits 8.5 percent annualised; resilient net profit equalled reported, so the earnings are not flattered. The risks research itself rates the joint probability of its bear case low to medium because of the structural hedging, and names the invalidation of its own thesis as maturing swaps shielding the margin during cuts, which is what the 2027 to 2028 roll does. So the record parks rather than shorts: a 20 percent de-rating would make the FALSE FRIEND reading and the record's case the same trade from opposite ends, a B case at 25 EUR. Against the "just buy the compounding" version it holds that the framework's bar is 20 percent, the multiple is industry-driven at the 92nd percentile, and a 20 percent de-rating is the modal outcome over three years for a bank whose rate tailwind is dated.
triggers: The Q3 2026 results (29 to 31 October 2026) are the first liability-margin test after a quarter of German deposit campaigns and decide whether sell-side momentum continues; the full-year results in late January 2027 carry the new finance director's first 2027 guidance.

Progress trigger: the shares toward 25 to 27 EUR (7.7x to 8.3x the current 24-month-forward earnings) with the liability margin at or above 1.05 percent and the Q3 2026 print confirming the German deposit defence. Drop trigger: the liability margin below 1.00 percent, or ING raising its standard German savings rate.

The liability margin: current 1.07 percent; guidance 100 to 110 basis points, the finance director expecting more than 110 in 2027; our modal case above 1.10 percent in 2027; Alarm below 1.05 percent; Invalidate below 1.00 percent. What would change our mind on the margin condition: a Q3 2026 margin below 1.05 percent or ING raising its standard German savings rate.
FY2028 earnings per share of about 3.35 EUR: what would change our mind is a 2027 cost guide above 13.3 billion EUR or Stage 2 migration in Dutch mortgages.

The held-multiple branch: what would change our mind toward it is the cohort median multiple holding above 9x through a first ECB cut. Alarm on the sector multiple: cohort median below 8.5x with ING unchanged; no Invalidate level, because the risk is the case's own entry level.
The rate path: Alarm ECB deposit rate below 2.25 percent; Invalidate a cut cycle to 2.0 percent with the liability margin below 1.00 percent.
